chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Al-Haysam ibn Abu Masrouq Al-Nahdi, from Maruk ibn Ubayd, from one of our companions, from Mansur ibn Hazim, who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'I used to go out in my youth to the outskirts with the youths of the neighborhood, and I was tested by striking a man with a stick and killing him.' He said, 'Did you know this matter (Wilayah) at that time?' I said, 'No.' He said to me, 'Your ignorance of this matter was more severe upon you than what you have entered into.'

key_terms.الْأَمْر: The matter (referring to Wilayah or divine authority)
key_terms.الْمُخَارَجَة: The outskirts or fields outside the city

ai.seo_question: What is the significance of knowing Wilayah in relation to one's sins and ignorance?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) highlights the pivotal role of *Wilayah* (divine authority) in determining the spiritual weight of sins, noting that Mansur ibn Hazim’s lack of knowledge of it during his youth was a heavier burden than the physical act of killing itself. This underscores the Shia scholarly view that ignorance of the Imamate is not merely an excuse but a fundamental deficiency in one's religious foundation, amplating the consequences of subsequent actions.
